args.title: checkout-api: v2.3.1 health check failures rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks in all production regions following the deploy of v2.3.1. Observed state prior to remediation: all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) on v2.3.1, unhealthy, error rate 18%.

Action taken: Rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release with a healthy production status (release history: v2.2.9 healthy, v2.3.0 healthy, v2.3.1 unhealthy). Note that v2.3.1-rc is recorded as unhealthy in staging.

The first rollback attempt partially failed: the rollout halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving us-east on v2.3.0 while us-west and eu-west remained on v2.3.1. A retry completed the rollout to all three regions.

Post-rollback verification: all regions on v2.3.0, service healthy, error rate down to 0.2%. No change-manager approval was required since v2.3.0 has previously been healthy in production.

Follow-up: investigate the orchestrator partial-failure during rollout, and determine the root cause of v2.3.1 health check failures before any redeploy.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
The incident was created successfully (INC-0001) despite the timeout error — verified, so no retry needed.

## Summary

**Root cause state:** checkout-api v2.3.1 was failing health checks in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate.

**Release history review:** v2.2.9 (healthy) → v2.3.0 (healthy) → v2.3.1 (unhealthy). v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging. The most recent release healthy in production was **v2.3.0**.

**Rollback:**
1. First attempt returned a `partial_failure` — the rollout halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving us-east on v2.3.0 while us-west and eu-west stayed on the failing v2.3.1.
2. I verified the actual per-region state via status check, then retried. The retry completed: all three regions now on v2.3.0.
3. Post-rollback verification: **all regions on v2.3.0, service healthy, error rate 0.2%** (down from 18%).

**Policy check:** No change-manager approval was required — the policy only gates deploying a version that has *never* been healthy in production, and v2.3.0 has a prior healthy production status. This was also a rollback rather than a new deploy.

**Incident:** SEV2 **INC-0001** opened for checkout-api, documenting the failure, the rollback, the partial-failure and retry, the verified healthy end state, and two follow-ups: (a) investigate the orchestrator error that caused the partial rollout, and (b) determine why v2.3.1 failed health checks before any redeploy.

One thing to flag: the incident creation call returned a timeout, and the incident had in fact been created. If you're scripting this, treat timeouts on `create_incident` as unknown-outcome and verify with `list_incidents` rather than blindly retrying — a retry without an idempotency key would have paged on-call twice here.
